Full-page templates

Rendering reuses an already compiled template. Compile + render builds it each time. Compilation measures template creation alone. All timing modes are shown below.

Times in microseconds (µs); lower is better. The difference compares Rust with Django. Jinja2 is shown where the same template syntax can be compared; the translated report uses Django-specific syntax.

Bakerydemo measurement notes ↗

Wagtail’s Bakerydemo brings third-party tags, includes, rich content, and database access into the comparison. The chart measures warm template rendering, not page load: it excludes the initial view execution, but includes work triggered during rendering; the full-request difference under each bar covers the whole view. These measurements come from a separate run on 2026-10-12, using Python 3.12.9 and Django 6.0.9.

2.3% less time for warm template rendering; 2.3% less time for server-side Django test-client requests. Geometric means of per-page median ratios.

250 samples per page and backend. Warm render includes UTF-8 encoding and work initiated by template tags. Requests include views, middleware, database work, and rendering; they exclude network transport. This recorded build is separate from the filter and page measurements above, and the timing control does not change these results.

How to read these results

Full-page, filter, and tag timings report the best of 7 samples, using the same calibrated call count for each engine. Template loaders are cached and contexts are created outside the timed loop. This measures template work, rather than complete HTTP requests.

Results depend on the template, inputs, Python version, and machine. Small differences may be timing noise. Bakerydemo uses medians from its own recorded run and is reported separately.
